notes: N097. How well can every pair of cell lineages be told apart from the PREDICTED markers? Scale: for lineages A and B with defining markers a and b, every cell gets the score z(predicted a) - z(predicted b) (z-score over all test cells); the tile is the AUROC of that score for A cells vs B cells = the probability that a randomly drawn A cell scores higher than a randomly drawn B cell. .5 = coin flip (not separable), .7 = weak, .8 = moderate, .9 = good, 1 = perfect. No classifier is fitted; the matrix is symmetric. a BSCCM, N085 record ensemble, mean of the 2 directions; lineages = positives of each marker on its own single-stain slide of the test draw. Range .82 (T vs B) to .99 (NK vs monocyte). Because the two lineages of a pair come from different slides, a slide control scores ALL cells of slide a vs ALL cells of slide b with the same score (same blood draw -> expected .5): mean |AUROC - .5| = 0.040, range 0.40-0.54 (lowest for pairs with the CD16 slide). b, c ImageStream sandbox (external dataset; all 9 markers measured on every cell; lineages = gates on the held-out donor's measured labels; mean of 3 held-out donors; N080 ResNet-50 models trained with all markers per cell (b) or one marker per cell (c), the BSCCM-like regime). The measured markers give AUROC 1.00 for every pair (by construction). Myeloid vs lymphoid pairs are separated well (.88-1.00); lymphocyte subsets are not: CD4 T vs CD8 T .65/.60, CD8 T vs NK .57/.65, B vs CD8 T .67/.73.
significance: two-sided; Holm-corrected over all comparisons of a panel (one family per panel); * <0.05 ** <0.01 *** <0.001 **** <0.0001
